text:
Pittsburgh arrives having lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah on Wednesday, a game where Logan Cooley scored three for the Mammoth and Mikhail Sergachev ended it. The Penguins are 2-2-1 in their last five and still without Bryan Rust, with Tommy Novak now on Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell's line. Montreal has won four straight, most recently 5-2 at Dallas, but is missing Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. The teams already met on Oct. 3, when MTL beat PIT 6-5 in overtime, a game our numbers say Pittsburgh deserved to win 44% of the time. Phillip Danault plays his 800th NHL game.

On chance quality, the sides are close. At five on five, PIT has taken 52% of the expected goals and MTL 54%. Montreal's trouble is discipline: 5.0 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. The goalie matchup is lopsided. Montreal's projected starter, Jacob Fowler, has saved 9.9 goals more than the shots he faced would predict this season (goals saved above expected). Pittsburgh's projected Sergei Murashov is at -1.9, and he starts over Arturs Silovs.

Cole Caufield is our top scoring pick at 38%, and as Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted, there's been "a lot of work on cross zone passes and one timers for Caufield and Hutson." Crosby is 30% to score and 58% for a point. Two under-the-radar names to watch: Montreal's Alexandre Texier, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (14% to score), and Pittsburgh's Ben Kindel, newly in the top six and 47% for a point.
